title.zh: 卷一百一十 列傳第六十: 李光弼 王思禮 鄧景山 辛雲京
title.en: Volume 110 Biographies 60: Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Deng Jingshan, Xin Yunjing
title.raw: 卷一百一十 列傳第六十: 李光弼 王思禮 鄧景山 辛雲京 Volume 110 Biographies 60: Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Deng Jingshan, Xin Yunjing

sentences.zh: 李光弼，營州柳城人。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi was a native of Liucheng in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi was from Liucheng in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先，契丹之酋長。

translations.literal: His ancestors were chieftains of the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had been chieftains of the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 父楷洛，開元初，左羽林將軍同正、朔方節度副使，封薊國公，以驍果聞。

translations.literal: His father Kailuo, at the beginning of Kaiyuan, was Left General of the Feathered Forest Guards with concurrent appointment and deputy military commissioner of Shuofang, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, and was known for martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kailuo, in the early Kaiyuan era, served as Left General of the Feathered Forest Guards with concurrent appointment and as deputy military commissioner of Shuofang; he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji and was famed for his martial valor.

sentences.zh: 光弼幼持節行，善騎射，能讀班氏《漢書》。

translations.literal: From youth Guangbi maintained integrity in conduct, was skilled at horseback archery, and could read Ban's Book of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Li Guangbi was upright in conduct, excelled at mounted archery, and could read Ban Gu's Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 少從戎，嚴毅有大略，起家左衛郎。

translations.literal: He entered military service young, was stern and resolute with great strategic vision, and began his career as a gentleman of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He took up arms while still young—stern, resolute, and far-sighted—and began his career as a gentleman of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，終喪不入妻室。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he observed mourning and did not enter his wife's chamber until the mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he observed the full mourning period and did not enter his wife's chamber until it was complete.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，累遷左清道率兼安北都護府、朔方都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was repeatedly promoted to Left Commandant of the Clear Way, concurrently serving the Protectorate General of Anbei and as chief inspector of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao era he rose through repeated promotions to Left Commandant of the Clear Way, concurrently holding appointments in the Protectorate General of Anbei and as chief inspector of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 五載，河西節度王忠嗣補為兵馬使，充赤水軍使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Wang Zhongsi, military commissioner of Hexi, appointed him army and horse commissioner and made him commander of the Chishui Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 5, Wang Zhongsi, military commissioner of Hexi, appointed him army and horse commissioner and assigned him to command the Chishui Army.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣遇之甚厚，常云：「光弼必居我位。」

translations.literal: Zhongsi treated him with great favor and often said: "Guangbi will surely occupy my position."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi treated him with exceptional generosity and often declared: "Guangbi will surely take my place."

sentences.zh: 邊上稱為名將。

translations.literal: On the frontier he was acclaimed as a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: He was acclaimed on the frontier as a renowned commander.

sentences.zh: 八載，充節度副使，封薊郡公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as deputy military commissioner and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 8 he served as deputy military commissioner and was enfeoffed Duke of Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十一載，拜單於副使都護。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed deputy commissioner and protector-general of Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 11 he was appointed deputy commissioner and protector-general of Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 十三載，朔方節度安思順奏為副使、知留後事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year An Sishun, military commissioner of Shuofang, memorialized to appoint him deputy commissioner and acting regent of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 13 An Sishun, military commissioner of Shuofang, memorialized the throne to appoint him deputy commissioner with control of circuit affairs as acting regent.

sentences.zh: 思順愛其材，欲妻之，光弼稱疾辭官。

translations.literal: Sishun admired his talent and wished to give him his daughter in marriage; Guangbi pleaded illness and resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Sishun admired his ability and wished to give him his daughter in marriage; Guangbi pleaded illness and resigned his office.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度哥舒翰聞而奏之，得還京師。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Longyou, heard of this and memorialized the throne; Guangbi was permitted to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Longyou, heard of this and memorialized the throne, and Guangbi was permitted to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，封常清、高仙芝戰敗，斬於潼關。

translations.literal: In the An Lushan rebellion, Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi were defeated in battle and beheaded at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: During the An Lushan rebellion, Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi were defeated in battle and executed at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 又以哥舒翰率師拒賊。

translations.literal: Geshu Han was then dispatched to lead troops against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han was then ordered to lead an army to resist the rebels.

sentences.zh: 尋命郭子儀為朔方節度，收兵河西。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Guo Ziyi was appointed military commissioner of Shuofang and gathered troops in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Guo Ziyi was appointed military commissioner of Shuofang and gathered troops in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 玄宗眷求良將，委以河北、河東之事，以問子儀，子儀薦光弼堪當閫寄。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong eagerly sought able generals and entrusted him with affairs in Hebei and Hedong; he asked Ziyi, and Ziyi recommended Guangbi as fit to bear military command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong eagerly sought able generals and entrusted the affairs of Hebei and Hedong to him; he asked Ziyi, and Ziyi recommended Guangbi as fit to bear military command.

sentences.zh: 十五載正月，以光弼為雲中太守，攝御史大夫，充河東節度副使、知節度事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year Guangbi was made prefect of Yunzhong, acting censor-in-chief, and deputy military commissioner of Hedong with control of circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year Guangbi was appointed prefect of Yunzhong, acting censor-in-chief, and deputy military commissioner of Hedong with control of circuit affairs.

sentences.zh: 二月，轉魏郡太守、河北道采訪使，以朔方兵五千會郭子儀軍，東下井陘，收常山郡。

translations.literal: In the second month he was transferred to prefect of Wei Commandery and Hebei circuit inspector; with five thousand Shuofang troops he joined Guo Ziyi's army, marched east through Jingxing Pass, and recovered Changshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was transferred to prefect of Wei Commandery and Hebei circuit inspector; with five thousand Shuofang troops he joined Guo Ziyi's army, marched east through Jingxing Pass, and recovered Changshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 賊將史思明以卒數萬來援常山，追擊破之，進收槁城等十餘縣，南攻趙郡。

translations.literal: The rebel general Shi Siming came with tens of thousands of troops to relieve Changshan; Guangbi pursued, defeated him, advanced to recover more than ten counties including Gaocheng, and attacked Zhaojun to the south.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Shi Siming came with tens of thousands of troops to relieve Changshan; Guangbi pursued and defeated him, then advanced to recover more than ten counties including Gaocheng and attacked Zhaojun to the south.

sentences.zh: 三月八日，光弼兼范陽長史、河北節度使，拔趙郡。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the third month Guangbi was additionally made chief administrator of Fanyang and military commissioner of Hebei; he captured Zhaojun.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the third month Guangbi was additionally appointed chief administrator of Fanyang and military commissioner of Hebei and captured Zhaojun.

sentences.zh: 自祿山反，常山為戰場，死人蔽野，光弼酹其屍而哭之，為賊幽閉者出之，誓平寇難，以慰其心。

translations.literal: Since An Lushan's rebellion Changshan had been a battlefield and the dead covered the fields; Guangbi poured libations before the corpses and wept over them, released those imprisoned by the rebels, and swore to suppress the calamity of banditry to console the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Since An Lushan's rebellion Changshan had been a battlefield and the dead covered the fields; Guangbi poured libations before the corpses and wept, released those imprisoned by the rebels, and swore to suppress the rebels and console the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 六月，與賊將蔡希德、史思明、尹子奇戰於常山郡之嘉山，大破賊黨，斬首萬計，生擒四千。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he fought rebel generals Cai Xide, Shi Siming, and Yin Ziqi at Jiashan in Changshan Commandery, routed the rebel host, beheaded enemies numbering in the tens of thousands, and captured four thousand alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he fought rebel generals Cai Xide, Shi Siming, and Yin Ziqi at Jiashan in Changshan Commandery, routed the rebels, beheaded tens of thousands, and captured four thousand alive.

sentences.zh: 思明露發跣足，奔於博陵。

translations.literal: Siming, with hair loose and barefoot, fled to Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Siming fled to Boling with hair loose and barefoot.

sentences.zh: 河北歸順者十餘郡。

translations.literal: More than ten commanderies in Hebei submitted.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten commanderies in Hebei submitted to the court.

sentences.zh: 光弼以范陽祿山之巢穴，將先斷之，使將絕根本。

translations.literal: Guangbi considered Fanyang the rebels' lair under An Lushan and intended first to sever it, thereby cutting off their root.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi regarded Fanyang as An Lushan's base and intended to cut it off first, thereby severing the rebels at the root.

sentences.zh: 會哥舒翰潼關失守，玄宗幸蜀，人心驚駭。

translations.literal: Just then Geshu Han lost Tong Pass, Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu, and men's hearts were stricken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Geshu Han lost Tong Pass, Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu, and the people were stricken with terror.

sentences.zh: 肅宗理兵於靈武，遣中使劉智達追光弼、子儀赴行在，授光弼戶部尚書，兼太原尹、北京留守、同中書門下平章事，以景城、河間之卒五千赴太原。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong organized troops at Lingwu, sent the inner envoy Liu Zhida to summon Guangbi and Ziyi to the imperial camp, appointed Guangbi Minister of Revenue, concurrently Mayor of Taiyuan, defender of the Northern Capital, and Grand Councilor, and sent five thousand troops from Jingcheng and Hejian to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong organized troops at Lingwu, sent the inner envoy Liu Zhida to summon Guangbi and Ziyi to the imperial camp, appointed Guangbi Minister of Revenue with concurrent posts as Mayor of Taiyuan, defender of the Northern Capital, and Grand Councilor, and sent five thousand troops from Jingcheng and Hejian to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時節度王承業軍政不修，詔御史崔眾交兵於河東。

translations.literal: At that time the military commissioner Wang Chengye did not maintain military discipline; an edict ordered the censor Cui Zhong to transfer troops in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Military Commissioner Wang Chengye did not maintain military discipline, and an edict ordered Censor Cui Zhong to transfer troops in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 眾侮易承業，或裹甲持槍，突入承業廳事玩謔之。

translations.literal: Zhong treated Chengye with contempt; some wrapped in armor and bearing spears burst into Chengye's main hall to mock and jest at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong treated Chengye with contempt; some men in armor bearing spears burst into Chengye's main hall to mock him.

sentences.zh: 光弼聞之素不平。

translations.literal: Guangbi had long been displeased upon hearing of this.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi had long been displeased when he heard of this.

sentences.zh: 至是，交眾兵於光弼。

translations.literal: At this time Zhong's troops were transferred to Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Zhong's troops were transferred to Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 眾以麾下來，光弼出迎，旌旗相接而不避。

translations.literal: Zhong came with his subordinates; Guangbi went out to receive him, their banners and flags meeting head-on without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong came with his subordinates; Guangbi went out to receive him, their banners meeting head-on without yielding.

sentences.zh: 光弼怒其無禮，又不即次兵，令收系之。

translations.literal: Guangbi, angered at his discourtesy and that he did not immediately halt his troops, ordered him seized and bound.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi, angered at his discourtesy and that he did not immediately halt his troops, ordered him seized and bound.

sentences.zh: 頃中使至，除眾御史中丞，懷其敕問眾所在。

translations.literal: Shortly an inner envoy arrived appointing Zhong Vice Censor-in-Chief; bearing the edict he asked where Zhong was.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly an inner envoy arrived with an appointment making Zhong Vice Censor-in-Chief; bearing the edict he asked where Zhong was.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「眾有罪，系之矣！」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "Zhong is guilty—I have bound him!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said: "Zhong is guilty—I have bound him!"

sentences.zh: 中使以敕示光弼，光弼曰：「今只斬侍御史；

translations.literal: The envoy showed the edict to Guangbi; Guangbi said: "For now I would behead only the Attending Censor;
translations.idiomatic: The envoy showed the edict to Guangbi; Guangbi said: "For now I would behead only the Attending Censor;

sentences.zh: 若宣制命，即斬中丞；

translations.literal: if you proclaim the formal appointment, I will behead the Vice Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: if you proclaim the formal appointment, I will behead the Vice Censor-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 若拜宰相，亦斬宰相。」

translations.literal: if he is appointed Grand Councilor, I will behead the Grand Councilor as well."
translations.idiomatic: if he is appointed Grand Councilor, I will behead the Grand Councilor as well."

sentences.zh: 中使懼，遂寢之而還。

translations.literal: The envoy was afraid and let the matter drop and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was afraid, let the matter drop, and returned.

sentences.zh: 翌日，以兵仗圍眾，至碑堂下斬之，威震三軍。

translations.literal: The next day he surrounded Zhong with armed troops and beheaded him below the stele hall; awe shook the entire army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he surrounded Zhong with armed troops and beheaded him below the stele hall, and awe shook the entire army.

sentences.zh: 命其親屬吊之。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhong's kin to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhong's relatives to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 二年，賊將史思明、蔡希德、高秀巖、牛廷玠等四偽帥率眾十餘萬來攻太原。

translations.literal: In the second year the rebel generals Shi Siming, Cai Xide, Gao Xiuyan, and Niu Tingjie, four pretender commanders, led more than a hundred thousand men to attack Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the rebel generals Shi Siming, Cai Xide, Gao Xiuyan, and Niu Tingjie—four pretender commanders—led more than a hundred thousand men to attack Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 光弼經河北苦戰，精兵盡赴朔方，麾下皆烏合之眾，不滿萬人。

translations.literal: Guangbi had fought hard through Hebei; his elite troops had all gone to Shuofang, and those under his command were a mob of less than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi had fought hard through Hebei; his elite troops had all gone to Shuofang, and those under his command were a hastily gathered force of fewer than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 思明謂諸將曰：「光弼之兵寡弱，可屈指而取太原，鼓行而西，圖河隴、朔方，無後顧矣！」

translations.literal: Siming said to his generals: "Guangbi's troops are few and weak; Taiyuan can be taken at a finger's count; march west with drums beating, aim at Hexi, Longyou, and Shuofang, and we need look to nothing behind us!"
translations.idiomatic: Siming said to his generals: "Guangbi's troops are few and weak; Taiyuan can be taken at a finger's count; march west with drums beating, aim at Hexi, Longyou, and Shuofang, and we need look to nothing behind us!"

sentences.zh: 光弼所部將士聞之皆懼，議欲修城以待之，光弼曰：「城周四十里，賊垂至，今興功役，是未見敵而自疲矣。」

translations.literal: Guangbi's officers and men heard this and were all afraid; they discussed repairing the walls to await the enemy. Guangbi said: "The wall circuit is forty li; the enemy is nearly upon us—if we now begin public works, we will weary ourselves before we have seen the foe."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi's officers and men heard this and were all afraid; they discussed repairing the walls to await the enemy. Guangbi said: "The wall circuit is forty li; the enemy is nearly upon us—if we now begin public works, we will weary ourselves before we have seen the foe."

sentences.zh: 乃躬率士卒百姓外城掘壕以自固。

translations.literal: He then personally led soldiers and commoners to dig trenches outside the outer wall to strengthen their defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then personally led soldiers and commoners to dig trenches outside the outer wall to strengthen their defenses.

sentences.zh: 作塹數十萬，眾莫知所用。

translations.literal: Trenchworks numbering in the hundreds of thousands were made; the multitude did not know their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Trenches numbering in the hundreds of thousands were dug; the troops did not know their purpose.

sentences.zh: 及賊攻城於外，光弼即令增壘於內，環輒補之。

translations.literal: When the rebels attacked the city from outside, Guangbi immediately ordered ramparts added inside, repairing them in succession around the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked from outside the city, Guangbi immediately ordered ramparts added inside and repaired them in succession around the circuit.

sentences.zh: 賊城外詬詈戲侮者，光弼令穿地道，一夕而擒之，自此賊將行皆視地，不敢逼城。

translations.literal: Those among the rebels outside the walls who cursed and mocked in sport—Guangbi ordered tunnels dug, and in one night they were captured; thereafter rebel generals watched the ground as they walked and did not dare press close to the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels outside the walls who cursed and mocked in sport—Guangbi ordered tunnels dug, and in one night they were captured; thereafter rebel generals watched the ground as they walked and did not dare press close to the walls.

sentences.zh: 強弩發石以擊之，賊驍將勁卒死者十二三。

translations.literal: With powerful crossbows and catapult stones they struck the enemy; two or three tenths of the rebels' fierce generals and crack troops died.
translations.idiomatic: With powerful crossbows and catapult stones they struck the enemy; two or three tenths of the rebels' fierce generals and crack troops were killed.

sentences.zh: 城中長幼鹹伏其勤智，懦兵增氣而皆欲出戰。

translations.literal: Old and young in the city all admired his diligence and wisdom; timid soldiers gained spirit and all wished to sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: Old and young in the city all admired his diligence and wisdom; timid soldiers gained spirit and all wished to sally forth to fight.

sentences.zh: 史思明揣知之，先歸，留蔡希德等攻之。

translations.literal: Shi Siming perceived this and withdrew first, leaving Cai Xide and others to continue the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming perceived this and withdrew first, leaving Cai Xide and others to continue the attack.

sentences.zh: 月餘，我怒而寇怠，光弼率敢死之士出擊，大破之，斬首七萬餘級，軍資器械一皆委棄。

translations.literal: After more than a month, our side was fierce while the invaders slackened; Guangbi led dare-to-die troops in a sally and routed them, beheading more than seventy thousand; military supplies, weapons, and equipment were all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month our side was fierce while the invaders slackened; Guangbi led dare-to-die troops in a sally and routed them, beheading more than seventy thousand; military supplies, weapons, and equipment were all abandoned.

sentences.zh: 賊始至及遁，五十餘日，光弼設小幕，宿於城東南隅，有急即應，行過府門，未嘗回顧。

translations.literal: From the rebels' arrival until their flight, more than fifty days—Guangbi set up a small tent and lodged in the southeast corner of the city; when there was urgency he responded at once; passing the prefectural gate he never once looked back.
translations.idiomatic: From the rebels' arrival until their flight, more than fifty days—Guangbi set up a small tent and lodged in the southeast corner of the city; when there was urgency he responded at once, and passing the prefectural gate he never once looked back.

sentences.zh: 賊退三日，決軍事畢，始歸府第。

translations.literal: Three days after the rebels withdrew, when military affairs were settled, he at last returned to his official residence.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after the rebels withdrew, once military affairs were settled, he at last returned to his official residence.

sentences.zh: 轉檢校司徒，收清夷、橫野等軍，擒賊將李弘義以歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Minister of Works, gathered the Qingyi and Hengye armies and others, and captured the rebel general Li Hongyi and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Acting Minister of Works, gathered the Qingyi and Hengye armies and others, captured the rebel general Li Hongyi, and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「銀青光祿大夫、檢校司徒、兼戶部尚書、同中書門下平章事、兼御史大夫、鴻臚卿、太原尹、北京留守、河東節度副大使、薊國公光弼，全德挺生，英才間出，幹城禦侮，坐甲安邊。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Silver and Blue Light Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Minister of Revenue, Grand Councilor, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Minister of Ceremonies, Mayor of Taiyuan, Defender of the Northern Capital, deputy grand military commissioner of Hedong, Duke of Ji—Guangbi—complete in virtue and emergent among the age, a rare talent appearing between generations, a bulwark against insult, maintaining armor to pacify the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The Silver and Blue Light Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Minister of Revenue, Grand Councilor, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Minister of Ceremonies, Mayor of Taiyuan, Defender of the Northern Capital, deputy grand military commissioner of Hedong, Duke of Ji—Guangbi—complete in virtue and emergent in his age, a rare talent appearing between generations, a bulwark against insult, maintaining armor to pacify the frontier.

sentences.zh: 可守司空、兼兵部尚書、中書門下平章事，進封魏國公，食實封八百戶。」

translations.literal: He may serve as Minister of Works, concurrently Minister of War, Grand Councilor; advance in enfeoffment to Duke of Wei; with eight hundred households of substantive fief."
translations.idiomatic: He may serve as Minister of Works, concurrently Minister of War, and Grand Councilor; advance in enfeoffment to Duke of Wei; with eight hundred households of substantive fief."

sentences.zh: 初，光弼次汴州，聞思明悉眾且至，謂許叔冀曰：「大夫能守此城浹旬，我必將兵來救。」

translations.literal: Initially, when Guangbi was stationed at Bianzhou and heard Siming was coming with his entire force, he said to Xu Shuji: "Sir, if you can hold this city for ten days, I will surely bring troops to rescue you."
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Guangbi was stationed at Bianzhou and heard Siming was coming with his entire force, he said to Xu Shuji: "Sir, if you can hold this city for ten days, I will surely bring troops to rescue you."

sentences.zh: 叔冀曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: Shuji said: "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: Shuji said: "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 光弼還東京，思明至汴，叔冀與戰不利，遂與董秦、梁浦、劉從諫率眾降思明。

translations.literal: Guangbi returned to the Eastern Capital; Siming reached Bian; Shuji fought unfavorably and then, with Dong Qin, Liang Pu, and Liu Congjian, led his troops to surrender to Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi returned to the Eastern Capital; Siming reached Bian; Shuji fought unfavorably and then, with Dong Qin, Liang Pu, and Liu Congjian, led his troops to surrender to Siming.

sentences.zh: 賊勢甚熾，遣梁浦、劉從諫、田神功等將兵徇江淮，謂之曰：「收得其地，每人貢兩船玉帛。」

translations.literal: The rebel strength was very great; he dispatched Liang Pu, Liu Congjian, Tian Shenggong, and others to lead troops through Jianghuai, saying to them: "When you take the land, each man shall submit two boatloads of silks and treasures."
translations.idiomatic: The rebel strength was very great; he dispatched Liang Pu, Liu Congjian, Tian Shenggong, and others to lead troops through Jianghuai, saying to them: "When you take the land, each man shall submit two boatloads of silks and treasures."

sentences.zh: 思明乘勝而西。

translations.literal: Siming pressed his victory westward.
translations.idiomatic: Siming pressed his victory westward.

sentences.zh: 光弼整眾徐行，至洛，謂留守韋陟曰：「賊乘鄴下之勝，再犯王畿，按甲以挫其鋒，不利速戰。

translations.literal: Guangbi reorganized his troops and marched slowly; reaching Luoyang he said to the defender Wei Zhi: "The rebels, riding their victory below Ye, are again violating the imperial domain; hold armor to blunt their edge—swift battle is not advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi reorganized his troops and marched slowly; reaching Luoyang he said to the defender Wei Zhi: "The rebels, riding their victory below Ye, are again violating the imperial domain; hold armor to blunt their edge—swift battle is not advantageous.

sentences.zh: 洛城非禦備之所，公計若何？」

translations.literal: Luoyang is not a place for defense—what is your plan?"
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang is not a place for defense—what is your plan?"

sentences.zh: 陟曰：「加兵陜州，退守潼關，據險以待之，足挫其銳矣！」

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Reinforce Shanzhou, withdraw to Tong Pass, and hold perilous ground to await them—that will suffice to blunt their keen edge!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said: "Reinforce Shanzhou, withdraw to Tong Pass, and hold perilous ground to await them—that will suffice to blunt their keen edge!"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「此蓋兵家常勢，非用奇之策也。

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "That is the common military practice, not a strategy employing the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said: "That is the common military practice, not a strategy employing the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 夫兩軍相寇，貴進尺寸之間耳。

translations.literal: When two armies contend, what matters is advancing by inches.
translations.idiomatic: When two armies contend, what matters is advancing inch by inch.

sentences.zh: 今委五百里而不顧，是張賊勢也。

translations.literal: Now to abandon five hundred li without a glance is to magnify the rebels' strength.
translations.idiomatic: Now to abandon five hundred li without a glance is to magnify the rebels' strength.

sentences.zh: 若移軍河陽，北阻澤潞、三城以抗，勝則擒之，敗則自守，表裏相應，使賊不敢西侵，此則猿臂之勢也。

translations.literal: If we shift the army to Heyang, with Ze and Lu and the Three Cities blocking to the north to resist—if we win we capture them, if we lose we hold ourselves; inner and outer respond to each other, so the rebels dare not invade west—this would be an ape's-arm posture.
translations.idiomatic: If we shift the army to Heyang, with Ze, Lu, and the Three Cities blocking to the north—if we win we capture them, if we lose we hold ourselves; inner and outer respond to each other so the rebels dare not invade west—this would be an ape's-arm posture.

sentences.zh: 夫辨朝廷之禮，光弼不如公；

translations.literal: In distinguishing court ritual, Guangbi is not the equal of you, sir;
translations.idiomatic: In distinguishing court ritual, Guangbi is not your equal, sir;

sentences.zh: 論軍旅之事，公不如光弼。」

translations.literal: in discussing military affairs, you, sir, are not the equal of Guangbi."
translations.idiomatic: in discussing military affairs, you, sir, are not Guangbi's equal."

sentences.zh: 陟無以應。

translations.literal: Zhi had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had no reply.

sentences.zh: 判官韋損曰：「東京帝宅，侍中何不守之？」

translations.literal: Adjutant Wei Sun said: "The Eastern Capital is the imperial residence—why, Vice Director, do you not defend it?"
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Wei Sun said: "The Eastern Capital is the imperial residence—why, Vice Director, do you not defend it?"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「若守洛城，汜水、崿嶺皆須人守，子為兵馬判官，能守之乎？」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "If we defend Luoyang, Sishui and Eling would both require men to guard them—you are the army and horse adjutant; could you guard them?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said: "If we defend Luoyang, Sishui and Eling would both require men to guard them—you are the army and horse adjutant; could you guard them?"

sentences.zh: 遂移牒留守及河南尹並留司官、坊市居人，出城避寇，空其城，率軍士運油鐵諸物，以為戰守之備。

translations.literal: He then issued orders to the defender, the Henan prefect, all remaining officials, and residents of wards and markets to leave the city to avoid the rebels, emptied the city, and led soldiers to transport oil, iron, and other materials for preparations of battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued orders to the defender, the Henan prefect, all remaining officials, and residents of wards and markets to leave the city to avoid the rebels, emptied the city, and led soldiers to transport oil, iron, and other materials for battle and defense.

sentences.zh: 時史思明已至偃師，光弼悉軍赴河陽。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Siming had already reached Yanshi; Guangbi led his entire army to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shi Siming had already reached Yanshi; Guangbi led his entire army to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 賊已至洛城，光弼軍方至石橋。

translations.literal: The rebels had already reached Luoyang when Guangbi's army had only reached Shiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already reached Luoyang when Guangbi's army had only reached Shiqiao.

sentences.zh: 日暮，令秉炬徐行，與賊相隨，而不敢來犯。

translations.literal: At dusk he ordered torches carried and marched slowly, following alongside the rebels yet they did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he ordered torches carried and marched slowly, following alongside the rebels, yet they did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 乙夜，入河陽三城。

translations.literal: At the second watch he entered the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch he entered the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 排閱守備，號令嚴明，與士卒同甘苦，鹹誓力戰。

translations.literal: He inspected the defenses, his commands were strict and clear, he shared hardship with the soldiers, and all swore to fight with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the defenses, his commands were strict and clear, he shared hardship with the soldiers, and all swore to fight with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 賊憚光弼威略，頓兵白馬寺，南不出百里，西不敢犯宮闕，於河陽南築月城，掘壕以拒光弼。

translations.literal: The rebels feared Guangbi's prestige and strategy; they halted at Baima Temple, did not advance south of a hundred li, did not dare west to violate the palace precincts, and south of Heyang built crescent ramparts and dug trenches to resist Guangbi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels feared Guangbi's prestige and strategy; they halted at Baima Temple, did not advance south of a hundred li, did not dare west to violate the palace precincts, and south of Heyang built crescent ramparts and dug trenches to resist Guangbi.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊攻城。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the rebels attacked the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels attacked the city.

sentences.zh: 於中潬城西大破逆黨五千餘眾，斬首千餘級，生擒五百餘人，溺死者大半。

translations.literal: West of Zhongtan City he routed more than five thousand of the rebel host, beheaded more than a thousand, captured more than five hundred alive, and more than half drowned.
translations.idiomatic: West of Zhongtan City he routed more than five thousand rebels, beheaded more than a thousand, captured more than five hundred alive, and more than half drowned.

sentences.zh: 初，光弼謂李抱玉曰：「將軍能為我守南城二日乎？」

translations.literal: Initially Guangbi said to Li Baoyu: "General, can you hold the south city for me for two days?"
translations.idiomatic: Initially Guangbi said to Li Baoyu: "General, can you hold the south city for me for two days?"

sentences.zh: 抱玉曰：「過期若何？」

translations.literal: Baoyu said: "If the time passes, then what?"
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu said: "If the time passes, then what?"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「過期而救不至，任棄也。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "If rescue does not come when the time passes, you may abandon it."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said: "If rescue does not come when the time passes, you may abandon it."

sentences.zh: 抱玉稟命，勒兵守南城，將陷，抱玉紿賊曰：「吾糧盡，明日當降。」

translations.literal: Baoyu received the order, drilled his troops and defended the south city; when it was about to fall, Baoyu deceived the rebels, saying: "My grain is exhausted; tomorrow I shall surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu received the order, drilled his troops and defended the south city; when it was about to fall, Baoyu deceived the rebels, saying: "My grain is exhausted; tomorrow I shall surrender."

sentences.zh: 賊眾大喜，斂軍以俟之。

translations.literal: The rebel host rejoiced greatly and drew in their troops to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel host rejoiced greatly and drew in their troops to wait.

sentences.zh: 抱玉復得繕完設備，明日，堅壁請戰。

translations.literal: Baoyu was again able to repair and complete his defenses; the next day he shut the gates and requested battle.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu was again able to repair and complete his defenses; the next day he shut the gates and requested battle.

sentences.zh: 賊怒見欺，急攻之。

translations.literal: The rebels, angered at being deceived, attacked urgently.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, angered at being deceived, attacked urgently.

sentences.zh: 抱玉出奇兵，表裏夾擊，殺傷甚眾，賊帥周摯領軍而退。

translations.literal: Baoyu sent out surprise troops and struck from inner and outer sides; many were killed and wounded; the rebel commander Zhou Zhi led his army in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu sent out surprise troops and struck from inner and outer sides; many were killed and wounded, and the rebel commander Zhou Zhi led his army in retreat.

sentences.zh: 光弼自將於中潬城，城外置柵，柵外大掘塹，闊二丈，深亦如之。

translations.literal: Guangbi personally commanded at Zhongtan City; outside the city he set palisades, and outside the palisades dug a great trench two zhang wide and equally deep.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi personally commanded at Zhongtan City; outside the city he set palisades, and outside the palisades dug a great trench two zhang wide and equally deep.

sentences.zh: 周摯舍南城，並力攻中潬。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhi abandoned the south city and combined forces to attack Zhongtan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi abandoned the south city and combined forces to attack Zhongtan.

sentences.zh: 光弼命荔非元禮出勁卒於羊馬城以拒賊。

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered Li Feiyuanli to send crack troops out from the sheep-and-horse rampart to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi ordered Li Feiyuanli to send crack troops out from the sheep-and-horse rampart to resist the rebels.

sentences.zh: 光弼於城東北角樹小紅旗，下望賊軍。

translations.literal: Guangbi set up a small red flag at the northeast corner of the city and looked down at the rebel army.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi set up a small red flag at the northeast corner of the city and looked down at the rebel army.

sentences.zh: 賊恃眾直逼其城，以車二乘載木鵝、蒙沖、鬥樓、橦車隨其後，督兵填城下塹，三面各八道過其兵，又當塹開柵，各置一門。

translations.literal: The rebels, relying on their numbers, pressed straight to the wall; two carts carrying wooden geese, covered assault boats, fighting towers, and battering rams followed behind; they drove the troops to fill the trench below the wall; on three sides eight passages each carried their troops across; they also opened palisades across the trench, each with one gate.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, relying on their numbers, pressed straight to the wall; two carts carrying wooden geese, covered assault boats, fighting towers, and battering rams followed behind; they drove troops to fill the trench below the wall; on three sides eight passages each carried their troops across; they also opened palisades across the trench, each with one gate.

sentences.zh: 光弼遙望賊逼城，使人語荔非元禮曰：「中丞看賊填塹開柵過兵，居然不顧，何也？」

translations.literal: Guangbi, watching from afar as the rebels pressed the wall, sent someone to say to Li Feiyuanli: "Vice Director, you see the rebels filling the trench and opening palisades to pass troops, yet pay no heed—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi, watching from afar as the rebels pressed the wall, sent someone to say to Li Feiyuanli: "Vice Director, you see the rebels filling the trench and opening palisades to pass troops, yet pay no heed—why?"

sentences.zh: 元禮報曰：「太尉擬守乎，擬戰乎？」

translations.literal: Yuanli replied: "Grand Marshal, do you intend to defend or to fight?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli replied: "Grand Marshal, do you intend to defend or to fight?"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「戰。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "Fight."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said: "Fight."

sentences.zh: 元禮曰：「若戰，賊為我填塹，復何嫌也！」

translations.literal: Yuanli said: "If we fight, the rebels are filling the trench for us—what is there to dislike!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli said: "If we fight, the rebels are filling the trench for us—what is there to dislike!"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「吾智不及公，公其勉之！」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "My wisdom does not match yours—do your utmost!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said: "My wisdom does not match yours—do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 元禮俟柵開，率其勇敢出戰，一逼賊軍，退走數百步。

translations.literal: Yuanli waited until the palisade opened, led his brave men out to fight, pressed the rebel army once, and withdrew several hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli waited until the palisade opened, led his brave men out to fight, pressed the rebel army once, and withdrew several hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 元禮料敵陣堅，雖出處馳突，不足破賊，收軍稍退，以怠其寇而攻之。

translations.literal: Yuanli judged the enemy formation firm; though he charged in and out, it was insufficient to break the rebels; he withdrew his troops slightly to slacken the invaders and then attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli judged the enemy formation firm; though he charged in and out, it was insufficient to break the rebels; he withdrew his troops slightly to slacken the invaders and then attack.

sentences.zh: 光弼望見收軍，大怒，使人喚元禮，欲按軍令。

translations.literal: Guangbi saw the withdrawal and was greatly angered; he sent someone to summon Yuanli, intending to enforce military law.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi saw the withdrawal and was greatly angered; he sent someone to summon Yuanli, intending to enforce military law.

sentences.zh: 元禮曰：「戰正忙，喚作何物？」

translations.literal: Yuanli said: "The battle is busy—what are you calling me for?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli said: "The battle is busy—what are you calling me for?"

sentences.zh: 良久，令軍中鼓噪出柵門，徒搏齊進，賊大潰。

translations.literal: After a long while he ordered the army to drum and shout and go out through the palisade gate; they closed in hand to hand and the rebels were routed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he ordered the army to drum and shout and go out through the palisade gate; they closed in hand to hand and the rebels were routed in great disorder.

sentences.zh: 周摯復整軍押北城而下，將攻之。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhi again reorganized his army and pressed down from the north city, about to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhi again reorganized his army and pressed down from the north city, about to attack.

sentences.zh: 光弼遽率眾入北城，登城望曰：「彼雖眾，亂而囂，不足懼也。

translations.literal: Guangbi hastily led his troops into the north city, ascended the wall, looked out, and said: "Though they are many, they are disorderly and clamorous—not to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi hastily led his troops into the north city, ascended the wall, looked out, and said: "Though they are many, they are disorderly and clamorous—not to be feared.

sentences.zh: 當為公等日午而破之。」

translations.literal: I shall break them for you at midday."
translations.idiomatic: I shall break them for you at midday."

sentences.zh: 命出將戰。

translations.literal: He ordered the generals out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the generals out to fight.

sentences.zh: 及期，不決，謂諸將曰：「向來戰，何處最堅而難犯？」

translations.literal: When the time came and there was no decision, he said to the generals: "In the fighting just now, where was strongest and hardest to breach?"
translations.idiomatic: When the time came and there was no decision, he said to the generals: "In the fighting just now, where was strongest and hardest to breach?"

sentences.zh: 或曰：「西北角。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "The northwest corner."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "The northwest corner."

sentences.zh: 遽命郝玉曰：「爾往擊之。」

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Hao Yu: "You go strike it."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Hao Yu: "You go strike it."

sentences.zh: 玉曰：「玉，步卒也，請騎軍五百翼之。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "Yu is an infantryman; I request five hundred cavalry to flank me."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said: "Yu is an infantryman; I request five hundred cavalry to flank me."

sentences.zh: 光弼與之三百。

translations.literal: Guangbi gave him three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi gave him three hundred.

sentences.zh: 又問：「何處最堅？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "Where was strongest?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again: "Where was strongest?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「東南隅。」

translations.literal: They said: "The southeast corner."
translations.idiomatic: They said: "The southeast corner."

sentences.zh: 即命論惟貞以所部往擊之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Lun Weizhen to lead his command and strike it.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Lun Weizhen to lead his command and strike it.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「貞，蕃將也，不知步戰，請鐵騎三百。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Weizhen is a frontier general and does not know infantry fighting; I request three hundred iron cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Weizhen is a frontier general and does not know infantry fighting; I request three hundred iron cavalry."

sentences.zh: 與之百。

translations.literal: He gave him one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him one hundred.

sentences.zh: 光弼又出賜馬四十匹分給，且令之曰：「爾等望吾旗而戰，若麾旗緩，任爾觀望便宜；

translations.literal: Guangbi also brought out forty reward horses to distribute, and moreover ordered them: "You shall fight watching my flag; if I wave the flag slowly, you may observe and act as you see fit;
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi also brought out forty reward horses to distribute, and moreover ordered them: "You shall fight watching my flag; if I wave the flag slowly, you may observe and act as you see fit;

sentences.zh: 吾旗連麾三至地，則萬眾齊入，生死以之，少退者斬無舍。」

translations.literal: if my flag waves three times to the ground, then the whole host shall enter together; life and death by it—whoever retreats even slightly shall be beheaded without mercy."
translations.idiomatic: if my flag waves three times to the ground, then the whole host shall enter together; life and death by it—whoever retreats even slightly shall be beheaded without mercy."

sentences.zh: 玉策馬赴賊，有一人將援槍刺賊，洞馬腹，連刺數人；

translations.literal: Yu spurred his horse toward the rebels; one man was about to thrust with a spear and pierced a horse's belly, consecutively piercing several men;
translations.idiomatic: Yu spurred his horse toward the rebels; one man was about to thrust with a spear and pierced a horse's belly, consecutively piercing several men;

sentences.zh: 一人逢賊，不戰而退。

translations.literal: one man encountered the rebels and retreated without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: one man encountered the rebels and retreated without fighting.

sentences.zh: 光弼召不戰者斬，賞援槍者絹五百疋。

translations.literal: Guangbi summoned the one who did not fight and beheaded him; he rewarded the spear-thruster with five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi summoned the one who did not fight and beheaded him; he rewarded the spear-thruster with five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 須臾，郝玉奔歸。

translations.literal: In a moment Hao Yu came galloping back.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment Hao Yu came galloping back.

sentences.zh: 光弼望之，驚曰：「郝玉退，吾事危矣。」

translations.literal: Guangbi saw him and said in alarm: "Hao Yu has retreated—my affair is in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi saw him and said in alarm: "Hao Yu has retreated—my affair is in peril."

sentences.zh: 命左右取玉頭來。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to bring Yu's head.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to bring Yu's head.

sentences.zh: 玉見使者曰：「馬中箭，非敢敗也。」

translations.literal: Yu, seeing the messenger, said: "My horse was struck by an arrow—I did not dare fail."
translations.idiomatic: Yu, seeing the messenger, said: "My horse was struck by an arrow—I did not dare fail."

sentences.zh: 使者馳報，光弼令換馬遣之。

translations.literal: The messenger galloped back to report; Guangbi ordered a horse changed and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger galloped back to report; Guangbi ordered a horse changed and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 玉換馬復入，決死而前。

translations.literal: Yu changed horses and entered again, advancing resolved to die.
translations.idiomatic: Yu changed horses and entered again, advancing resolved to die.

sentences.zh: 光弼連麾，三軍望旗俱進，聲動天地，一鼓而賊大潰，斬萬餘級，生擒八千餘人，軍資器械糧儲數萬計，臨陣擒其大將徐璜玉、李秦授、周摯。

translations.literal: Guangbi waved his flag repeatedly; the three armies all advanced watching the flag; the sound shook heaven and earth; at one drum the rebels were routed in great disorder; more than ten thousand were beheaded, more than eight thousand captured alive, military supplies, weapons, grain, and stores numbered in the tens of thousands; on the battlefield he captured their great generals Xu Huangyu, Li Qinshou, and Zhou Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi waved his flag repeatedly; the three armies all advanced watching the flag; the sound shook heaven and earth; at one drum the rebels were routed in great disorder; more than ten thousand were beheaded, more than eight thousand captured alive, military supplies, weapons, grain, and stores numbered in the tens of thousands; on the battlefield he captured their great generals Xu Huangyu, Li Qinshou, and Zhou Zhi.

sentences.zh: 其大將安太清走保懷州。

translations.literal: Their great general An Taiqing fled to hold Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Their great general An Taiqing fled to hold Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 思明不知摯等敗，尚攻南城。

translations.literal: Siming did not know Zhi and the others had been defeated and was still attacking the south city.
translations.idiomatic: Siming did not know Zhi and the others had been defeated and was still attacking the south city.

sentences.zh: 光弼悉驅俘囚臨河以示之，殺數十人以威之，餘眾懼，投河赴南岸，光弼皆斬之。

translations.literal: Guangbi drove all the captives to the riverbank to show them, beheaded several tens to intimidate them; the rest were afraid and threw themselves into the river toward the south bank; Guangbi beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi drove all the captives to the riverbank to show them, beheaded several tens to intimidate them; the rest were afraid and threw themselves into the river toward the south bank; Guangbi beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 初，光弼將戰，謂左右曰：「戰，危事，勝負系之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Guangbi was about to fight, he said to those beside him: "Battle is a perilous affair; victory and defeat depend on it.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Guangbi was about to fight, he said to those beside him: "Battle is a perilous affair; victory and defeat depend on it.

sentences.zh: 光弼位為三公，不可死於賊手，茍事之不捷，繼之以死。」

translations.literal: Guangbi's rank is one of the Three Dukes; he cannot die at the rebels' hands; if the affair is not successful, I shall follow with death."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi's rank is one of the Three Dukes; he cannot die at the rebels' hands; if the affair is not successful, I shall follow with death."

sentences.zh: 及是擊賊，常納短刀於靴中，有決死之誌，城上面西拜舞，三軍感動。

translations.literal: At this time when he struck the rebels he constantly kept a short knife in his boot, with resolve to die; on the wall he bowed and danced facing west; the three armies were moved.
translations.idiomatic: At this time when he struck the rebels he constantly kept a short knife in his boot, with resolve to die; on the wall he bowed and danced facing west; the three armies were moved.

sentences.zh: 賊既敗走，光弼收懷州，思明來救，迎擊於沁水之上，又敗之。

translations.literal: After the rebels were defeated and fled, Guangbi recovered Huai Prefecture; Siming came to rescue; he met and struck them above the Qin River and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated and fled, Guangbi recovered Huai Prefecture; Siming came to rescue; he met and struck them above the Qin River and defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 城將安太清極力拒守，月餘不下。

translations.literal: The city commander An Taiqing resisted with all his strength; for more than a month it was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: The city commander An Taiqing resisted with all his strength; for more than a month it was not taken.

sentences.zh: 光弼令仆固懷恩、郝玉由地道而入，得其軍號，乃登陴大呼，我師同登，城遂拔。

translations.literal: Guangbi ordered Pugu Huai'en and Hao Yu to enter by tunnel, obtained their army signals, then ascended the ramparts and shouted loudly; our army ascended together and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi ordered Pugu Huai'en and Hao Yu to enter by tunnel, obtained their army signals, then ascended the ramparts and shouted loudly; our army ascended together and the city was taken.

sentences.zh: 生擒安太清、周摯、楊希文等，送於闕下，即日懷州平。

translations.literal: An Taiqing, Zhou Zhi, Yang Xiwen, and others were captured alive and sent to the court; on that same day Huai Prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: An Taiqing, Zhou Zhi, Yang Xiwen, and others were captured alive and sent to the court; on that same day Huai Prefecture was pacified.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵臨淮郡王，累加實封至一千五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced in rank to Prince of Linhuai Commandery; his substantive fief was cumulatively increased to one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was advanced in rank to Prince of Linhuai Commandery; his substantive fief was cumulatively increased to one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 觀軍容使魚朝恩屢言賊可滅之狀，朝旨令光弼速收東都。

translations.literal: The army-inspection commissioner Yu Chao'en repeatedly spoke of conditions in which the rebels could be destroyed; court orders commanded Guangbi to recover the Eastern Capital quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The army-inspection commissioner Yu Chao'en repeatedly spoke of conditions in which the rebels could be destroyed; court orders commanded Guangbi to recover the Eastern Capital quickly.

sentences.zh: 光弼屢表：「賊鋒尚銳，請候時而動，不可輕進。」

translations.literal: Guangbi repeatedly memorialized: "The rebels' edge is still keen; I ask to wait for the right moment and not advance lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi repeatedly memorialized: "The rebels' edge is still keen; I ask to wait for the right moment and not advance lightly."

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩又害光弼之功，潛附朝恩，言賊可滅。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en also resented Guangbi's merit; he secretly attached himself to Chao'en and said the rebels could be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en also resented Guangbi's merit; he secretly attached himself to Chao'en and said the rebels could be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 由是中使督戰，光弼不獲已，進軍列陣於北邙山下。

translations.literal: Thereupon inner envoys pressed for battle; Guangbi could not refuse and advanced his army, forming battle lines below Mount Beimang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon inner envoys pressed for battle; Guangbi could not refuse and advanced his army, forming battle lines below Mount Beimang.

sentences.zh: 賊悉精銳來戰，光弼敗績，軍資器械並為賊所有。

translations.literal: The rebels sent all their elite to fight; Guangbi was defeated; military supplies, weapons, and equipment all became the rebels' possession.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent all their elite to fight; Guangbi was defeated; military supplies, weapons, and equipment all fell into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 時李抱玉亦棄河陽，光弼渡河保聞喜。

translations.literal: At that time Li Baoyu also abandoned Heyang; Guangbi crossed the river and held Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Baoyu also abandoned Heyang; Guangbi crossed the river and held Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 朝旨以懷恩異同致敗，優詔征之。

translations.literal: Court orders held that Huai'en's dissent had caused the defeat; an edict of favor summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Court orders held that Huai'en's dissent had caused the defeat; an edict of favor summoned him.

sentences.zh: 光弼自河中入朝，抗表請罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: Guangbi entered court from Hezhong, submitted a memorial requesting punishment, and an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi entered court from Hezhong, submitted a memorial requesting punishment, and an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 光弼懇讓太尉，遂加開府儀同三司、侍中、河南尹、行營節度使；

translations.literal: Guangbi earnestly declined the post of Grand Marshal; he was then given Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same rank as the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, Henan Prefect, and campaign commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi earnestly declined the post of Grand Marshal; he was then given Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same rank as the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, Henan Prefect, and campaign commissioner;

sentences.zh: 俄復拜太尉，充河南、淮南、山南東道、荊南等副元帥，侍中如故，出鎮臨淮。

translations.literal: Shortly he was again appointed Grand Marshal, made deputy supreme commander of Henan, Huainan, the Eastern Circuit of Shannan, and Jingnan, Palace Attendant as before, and went out to garrison Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was again appointed Grand Marshal, made deputy supreme commander of Henan, Huainan, the Eastern Circuit of Shannan, and Jingnan, Palace Attendant as before, and went out to garrison Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 史朝義乘邙山之勝，寇申、光等十三州，自領精騎圍李岑於宋州。

translations.literal: Shi Chaoyi, riding the victory at Mount Beimang, raided thirteen prefectures including Shen and Guang; he personally led elite cavalry to besiege Li Cen at Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chaoyi, riding the victory at Mount Beimang, raided thirteen prefectures including Shen and Guang; he personally led elite cavalry to besiege Li Cen at Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 將士皆懼，請南保揚州，光弼徑赴徐州以鎮之，遣田神功擊敗之。

translations.literal: Officers and men were all afraid and requested to withdraw south to defend Yangzhou; Guangbi went straight to Xuzhou to stabilize the situation and dispatched Tian Shenggong to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men were all afraid and requested to withdraw south to defend Yangzhou; Guangbi went straight to Xuzhou to stabilize the situation and dispatched Tian Shenggong to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 浙東賊首袁晁攻剽郡縣，浙東大亂。

translations.literal: Yuan Chao, rebel leader of Zhedong, attacked and plundered commanderies and counties; Zhedong was in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chao, rebel leader of Zhedong, attacked and plundered commanderies and counties; Zhedong was in great disorder.

sentences.zh: 光弼分兵除討，克定江左，人心乃安。

translations.literal: Guangbi divided troops to suppress and pacify them, settled the lands east of the Yangzi, and the people's hearts were then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi divided troops to suppress and pacify them, settled the lands east of the Yangzi, and the people's hearts were then at ease.

sentences.zh: 初，光弼將止臨淮，在道舁疾而行。

translations.literal: Initially Guangbi intended to stop at Linhuai and was carried on a litter along the road because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Guangbi intended to stop at Linhuai and was carried on a litter along the road because of illness.

sentences.zh: 監軍使以袁晁方擾江淮，光弼兵少，請保潤州以避其鋒。

translations.literal: The army-supervising commissioner, because Yuan Chao was then disturbing Jianghuai and Guangbi had few troops, requested to hold Runzhou to avoid their edge.
translations.idiomatic: The army-supervising commissioner, because Yuan Chao was then disturbing Jianghuai and Guangbi had few troops, requested to hold Runzhou to avoid their edge.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「朝廷寄安危於我，今賊雖強，未測吾眾寡，若出其不意，當自退矣。」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "The court has entrusted its safety and peril to me; though the rebels are strong now, they cannot measure our numbers; if we strike where they do not expect it, they should withdraw of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said: "The court has entrusted its safety and peril to me; though the rebels are strong now, they cannot measure our numbers; if we strike where they do not expect it, they should withdraw of themselves."

sentences.zh: 遂徑往泗州。

translations.literal: He then went straight to Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then went straight to Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 光弼未至河南也，田神功平劉展後，逗留於揚府，尚衡、殷仲卿相攻於兗、鄆、來瑱旅拒於襄陽，朝廷患之。

translations.literal: Before Guangbi had reached Henan, after Tian Shenggong pacified Liu Zhan he lingered at Yang Prefecture; Shang Heng and Yin Zhongqing attacked each other at Yan and Yun; Lai Tian's brigade resisted at Xiangyang; the court was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Before Guangbi had reached Henan, after Tian Shenggong pacified Liu Zhan he lingered at Yang Prefecture; Shang Heng and Yin Zhongqing attacked each other at Yan and Yun; Lai Tian's brigade resisted at Xiangyang; the court was troubled by this.

sentences.zh: 及光弼輕騎至徐州，史朝義退走，田神功遽歸河南，尚衡、殷仲卿、來瑱皆懼其威名，相繼赴闕，

translations.literal: When Guangbi arrived at Xuzhou with a light cavalry escort, Shi Chaoyi withdrew; Tian Shenggong hastily returned to Henan; Shang Heng, Yin Zhongqing, and Lai Tian all feared his prestige and successively went to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi arrived at Xuzhou with a light cavalry escort, Shi Chaoyi withdrew; Tian Shenggong hastily returned to Henan; Shang Heng, Yin Zhongqing, and Lai Tian all feared his prestige and successively went to court.

sentences.zh: 進封臨淮王，賜鐵券，圖形淩煙閣。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Linhuai, granted an iron certificate, and his likeness was placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Linhuai, granted an iron certificate, and his likeness was placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃入寇京畿，代宗詔征天下兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde the Tibetans invaded the capital region; Emperor Daizong ordered troops summoned from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangde era the Tibetans invaded the capital region; Emperor Daizong ordered troops summoned from throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 光弼與程元振不協，遷延不至。

translations.literal: Guangbi was not in accord with Cheng Yuanzhen and delayed and did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi was not in accord with Cheng Yuanzhen and delayed and did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 十月，西戎犯京師，代宗幸陜。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the western barbarians violated the capital; Emperor Daizong fled to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the western barbarians violated the capital; Emperor Daizong fled to Shan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方倚光弼為援，恐成嫌疑，數詔問其母。

translations.literal: The court was then relying on Guangbi as support and feared suspicion would arise; it repeatedly issued edicts inquiring after his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then relying on Guangbi as support and feared suspicion would arise; it repeatedly issued edicts inquiring after his mother.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃退，乃除光弼東都留守，以察其去就。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans withdrew, Guangbi was appointed defender of the Eastern Capital to observe his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans withdrew, Guangbi was appointed defender of the Eastern Capital to observe his intentions.

sentences.zh: 光弼伺知之，辭以久待敕不至，且歸徐州，欲收江淮租賦以自給。

translations.literal: Guangbi perceived this; he declined on the grounds that he had long awaited an edict that did not come, and moreover returned to Xuzhou, intending to collect Jianghuai land taxes and grain levies to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi perceived this; he declined on the grounds that he had long awaited an edict that did not come, and moreover returned to Xuzhou, intending to collect Jianghuai land taxes and grain levies to supply himself.

sentences.zh: 代宗還京，二年正月，遣中使往宣慰。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong returned to the capital; in the first month of the second year he dispatched an inner envoy to offer consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong returned to the capital; in the first month of the second year he dispatched an inner envoy to offer consolation.

sentences.zh: 光弼母在河中，密詔子儀輿歸京師。

translations.literal: Guangbi's mother was in Hezhong; a secret edict ordered Ziyi to bring her by carriage to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi's mother was in Hezhong; a secret edict ordered Ziyi to bring her by carriage to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其弟光進，與李輔國同掌禁兵，委以心膂。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guangjin, together with Li Fuguo, jointly controlled the forbidden troops and was entrusted as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guangjin, together with Li Fuguo, jointly controlled the forbidden troops and was entrusted as a trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 至是，以光進為太子太保、兼御史大夫、涼國公、渭北節度使，上遇之益厚。

translations.literal: At this time Guangjin was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, Duke of Liang, and military commissioner of Weibei; the emperor treated him with still greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Guangjin was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, Duke of Liang, and military commissioner of Weibei; the emperor treated him with still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 光弼御軍嚴肅，天下服其威名，每申號令，諸將不敢仰視。

translations.literal: Guangbi commanded the army with strict discipline; the realm submitted to his prestige; whenever he issued commands the generals did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi commanded the army with strict discipline; the realm submitted to his prestige; whenever he issued commands the generals did not dare look up.

sentences.zh: 及懼朝恩之害，不敢入朝，田神功等皆不稟命，因愧恥成疾，遣衙將孫珍奉遺表自陳。

translations.literal: When he feared harm from Chao'en he did not dare enter court; Tian Shenggong and others all did not obey orders; because of shame and humiliation he fell ill; he sent his yamen general Sun Zhen to present a final memorial stating his case.
translations.idiomatic: When he feared harm from Chao'en he did not dare enter court; Tian Shenggong and others all did not obey orders; because of shame and humiliation he fell ill; he sent his yamen general Sun Zhen to present a final memorial stating his case.

sentences.zh: 七月，薨於徐州，時年五十七。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died at Xuzhou; he was then fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he died at Xuzhou; he was then fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日，贈太保，謚曰武穆。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor; his posthumous title was Wumu.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor; his posthumous title was Wumu.

sentences.zh: 光弼既疾亟，將吏問以後事，曰：「吾久在軍中，不得就養，既為不孝子，夫復何言！」

translations.literal: When Guangbi's illness was critical, the generals and officials asked about affairs after his death; he said: "I have long been in the army and could not go to support my parents; I am already an unfilial son—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi's illness was critical, the generals and officials asked about affairs after his death; he said: "I have long been in the army and could not go to support my parents; I am already an unfilial son—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 因取已封絹布各三千疋、錢三千貫文分給將士。

translations.literal: He then took already sealed silk and cloth, three thousand bolts each, and cash, three thousand strings, and distributed them to the generals and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He then took already sealed silk and cloth, three thousand bolts each, and cash, three thousand strings, and distributed them to the generals and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 部下護喪柩還京師。

translations.literal: His subordinates escorted the coffin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates escorted the coffin back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗遣中官開府魚朝恩吊問其母於私第，又命京兆尹第五琦監護喪事。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong dispatched the inner official Commissioner of the First Rank Yu Chao'en to offer condolences to his mother at her private residence, and also ordered the Henan prefect Diwu Qi to supervise the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong dispatched the inner official Commissioner of the First Rank Yu Chao'en to offer condolences to his mother at her private residence, and also ordered the Henan prefect Diwu Qi to supervise the funeral affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一月，葬於三原，詔宰臣百官祖送於延平門外。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was buried at Sanyuan; an edict ordered chief ministers and all officials to escort him in farewell outside Yanping Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was buried at Sanyuan; an edict ordered chief ministers and all officials to escort him in farewell outside Yanping Gate.

sentences.zh: 母李氏，有須數十莖，長五六寸，以子貴，封韓國太夫人，二子皆節制一品。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Li, had several dozen whiskers, five or six inches long; because of her son's eminence she was enfeoffed Grand Lady of Han; both sons held first-rank military commissionerships.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Li, had several dozen whiskers, five or six inches long; because of her son's eminence she was enfeoffed Grand Lady of Han; both sons held first-rank military commissionerships.

sentences.zh: 光弼十年間三入朝，與弟光進在京師，雖與光弼異母，性亦孝悌，雙旌在門，鼎味就養，甲第並開，往來追歡，極一時之榮。

translations.literal: Within ten years Guangbi entered court three times; he and his younger brother Guangjin were in the capital; though of a different mother from Guangbi, Guangjin was also filial and fraternal; double insignia at the gate, delicacies brought for their parents' support, grand mansions opened side by side—they came and went in mutual joy, reaching the summit of glory for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years Guangbi entered court three times; he and his younger brother Guangjin were in the capital; though of a different mother from Guangbi, Guangjin was also filial and fraternal; double insignia at the gate, delicacies brought for their parents' support, grand mansions opened side by side—they came and went in mutual joy, reaching the summit of glory for a time.

sentences.zh: 王思禮，營州城傍高麗人也。

translations.literal: Wang Sili was a native of Gaoli beside Yingzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sili was a native of Gaoli beside Yingzhou city.

sentences.zh: 父虔威，為朔方軍將，以習戰聞。

translations.literal: His father Qianwei was a general of the Shuofang Army and was known for mastery of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qianwei was a general of the Shuofang Army and was known for mastery of warfare.

sentences.zh: 思禮少習戎旅，隨節度使王忠嗣至河西，與哥舒翰對為押衙。

translations.literal: Sili from youth practiced military affairs; he followed Military Commissioner Wang Zhongsi to Hexi and paired with Geshu Han as commander's adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: Sili from youth practiced military affairs; he followed Military Commissioner Wang Zhongsi to Hexi and paired with Geshu Han as commander's adjutants.

sentences.zh: 及翰為隴右節度使，思禮與中郎周泌為翰押衙，以拔石堡城功，除右金吾衛將軍，充關西兵馬使，兼河源軍使。

translations.literal: When Han became military commissioner of Longyou, Sili and Central Gentleman Zhou Bi served as Han's commander's adjutants; for the merit of capturing Stone Fort City he was made General of the Right Golden Guard, army and horse commissioner of Guanxi, and concurrently commander of Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Han became military commissioner of Longyou, Sili and Central Gentleman Zhou Bi served as Han's commander's adjutants; for the merit of capturing Stone Fort City he was made General of the Right Golden Guard, army and horse commissioner of Guanxi, and concurrently commander of Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 十一載，加雲麾將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was given the additional title General of the Cloudy Pennant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was given the additional title General of the Cloudy Pennant.

sentences.zh: 十二載，翰征九曲，思禮後期，欲引斬之，續使命釋之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Han campaigned at Nine Bends; Sili was late; Han was about to have him beheaded; a follow-up envoy ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Han campaigned at Nine Bends; Sili was late; Han was about to have him beheaded; a follow-up envoy ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 思禮徐言曰：「斬則斬，卻喚何物？」

translations.literal: Sili said slowly: "Behead then behead—why call me back?"
translations.idiomatic: Sili said slowly: "Behead then behead—why call me back?"

sentences.zh: 諸將皆壯之。

translations.literal: All the generals admired him.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals admired him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，吐蕃蘇毗王款塞，詔翰至磨環川應接之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Tibetan Supi king came to the frontier in submission; an edict ordered Han to Mo Huan Chuan to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Tibetan Supi king came to the frontier in submission; an edict ordered Han to Mo Huan Chuan to receive him.

sentences.zh: 思禮墜馬損腳，翰謂中使李大宜曰：「思禮既損腳，更欲何之？」

translations.literal: Sili fell from his horse and injured his foot; Han said to the inner envoy Li Dayi: "Sili has already injured his foot—where does he think he is going?"
translations.idiomatic: Sili fell from his horse and injured his foot; Han said to the inner envoy Li Dayi: "Sili has already injured his foot—where does he think he is going?"

sentences.zh: 十四載六月，加金城太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he was given the additional post Prefect of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he was given the additional post Prefect of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，哥舒翰為元帥，奏思禮加開府儀同三司，兼太常卿同正員，充元帥府馬軍都將，每事獨與思禮決之。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, Geshu Han became supreme commander; he memorialized to give Sili Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same rank as the Three Excellencies, concurrently Minister of Ceremonies with regular appointment, and cavalry commander of the supreme commander's headquarters; in each affair he alone decided with Sili.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, Geshu Han became supreme commander; he memorialized to give Sili Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the same rank as the Three Excellencies, concurrently Minister of Ceremonies with regular appointment, and cavalry commander of the supreme commander's headquarters; in each affair he alone decided with Sili.

sentences.zh: 十五載二月，思禮白翰謀殺安思順父元貞，於紙隔上密語翰，請抗表誅楊國忠，翰不應。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year Sili told Han of a plan to kill An Sishun's father Yuanzhen; on a paper screen he whispered secretly to Han and requested to submit a memorial resisting and executing Yang Guozhong; Han did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year Sili told Han of a plan to kill An Sishun's father Yuanzhen; on a paper screen he whispered secretly to Han and requested to submit a memorial resisting and executing Yang Guozhong; Han did not respond.

sentences.zh: 復請以三十騎劫之，橫馱來潼關殺之，翰曰：「此乃翰反，何預祿山事。」

translations.literal: He again requested to use thirty horsemen to seize him, carry him across on horseback to Tong Pass and kill him; Han said: "This would be Han rebelling—what has it to do with Lushan's affair."
translations.idiomatic: He again requested to use thirty horsemen to seize him, carry him across on horseback to Tong Pass and kill him; Han said: "This would be Han rebelling—what has it to do with Lushan's affair."

sentences.zh: 六月，潼關失守，思禮西赴行在，至安化郡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Tong Pass was lost; Sili went west to the imperial camp and reached Anhua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Tong Pass was lost; Sili went west to the imperial camp and reached Anhua Commandery.

sentences.zh: 思禮與呂崇賁、李承光並引於纛下，責以不能堅守，並從軍令。

translations.literal: Sili, Lü Chongben, and Li Chengguang were all brought before the banner; they were charged with failing to hold firm and were all subject to military law.
translations.idiomatic: Sili, Lü Chongben, and Li Chengguang were all brought before the banner; they were charged with failing to hold firm and were all subject to military law.

sentences.zh: 或救之可收後效，遂斬承光而釋思禮、崇賁，與房琯為副使。

translations.literal: Someone pleaded that they could be spared to gather later merit; Chengguang was then beheaded while Sili and Chongben were released; he served as deputy to Fang Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Someone pleaded that they could be spared to gather later merit; Chengguang was then beheaded while Sili and Chongben were released; he served as deputy to Fang Guan.

sentences.zh: 便橋之戰又不利，除為關內節度使。

translations.literal: The Battle of Bian Bridge was again unfavorable; he was appointed military commissioner of Guannei.
translations.idiomatic: The Battle of Bian Bridge was again unfavorable; he was appointed military commissioner of Guannei.

sentences.zh: 尋遣守武功。

translations.literal: Shortly he was dispatched to defend Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was dispatched to defend Wugong.

sentences.zh: 賊將安守忠及李歸仁、安泰清來戰，思禮以其眾退守扶風。

translations.literal: The rebel generals An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, and An Taiqing came to fight; Sili withdrew his troops to defend Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel generals An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, and An Taiqing came to fight; Sili withdrew his troops to defend Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 賊兵分至大和關，去鳳翔五十里。

translations.literal: Rebel troops arrived separately at Dahe Pass, fifty li from Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel troops arrived separately at Dahe Pass, fifty li from Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 王師大駭，鳳翔戒嚴，中官及朝官皆出其孥，上使左右巡御史虞候書其名，乃止。

translations.literal: The imperial army was greatly alarmed; Fengxiang was placed under martial law; inner officials and court officials all sent out their wives and children; the emperor sent Left and Right Patrol Censors to record their names before it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army was greatly alarmed; Fengxiang was placed under martial law; inner officials and court officials all sent out their wives and children; the emperor sent Left and Right Patrol Censors to record their names before it stopped.

sentences.zh: 遂命司徒郭子儀以朔方之眾擊之而退。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Minister of Works Guo Ziyi to strike them with the Shuofang host and drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Minister of Works Guo Ziyi to strike them with the Shuofang host and drive them back.

sentences.zh: 九月，思禮從元帥廣平王收西京，既破賊，思禮領兵先入景清宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Sili followed the supreme commander the Prince of Guangping in recovering the Western Capital; after the rebels were broken Sili led troops first into Jingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Sili followed the supreme commander the Prince of Guangping in recovering the Western Capital; after the rebels were broken Sili led troops first into Jingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 又從子儀戰陜城、曲沃、新店，賊軍繼敗，收東京。

translations.literal: He again followed Ziyi in fighting at Shancheng, Quwo, and Xindian; the rebel army was repeatedly defeated and the Eastern Capital was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Ziyi in fighting at Shancheng, Quwo, and Xindian; the rebel army was repeatedly defeated and the Eastern Capital was recovered.

sentences.zh: 思禮又於絳郡破賊六千餘眾，器械山積，牛馬萬計。

translations.literal: Sili again at Jiang Commandery defeated more than six thousand rebels; weapons piled like mountains; cattle and horses numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Sili again at Jiang Commandery defeated more than six thousand rebels; weapons piled like mountains; cattle and horses numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部尚書、霍國公，食實封三百戶，

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue and Duke of Huo, with three hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue and Duke of Huo, with three hundred households of substantive fief.

sentences.zh: 與子儀等九節度圍安慶緒於相州。

translations.literal: Together with Ziyi and eight other military commissioners he besieged An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Ziyi and eight other military commissioners he besieged An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 思禮領關內及潞府行營步卒三萬、馬軍八千，大軍潰，唯思禮與李光弼兩軍獨全。

translations.literal: Sili commanded thirty thousand infantry of the Guannei and Lu Prefecture campaign forces and eight thousand cavalry; the great army was routed; only Sili's and Li Guangbi's two armies remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Sili commanded thirty thousand infantry of the Guannei and Lu Prefecture campaign forces and eight thousand cavalry; the great army was routed; only Sili's and Li Guangbi's two armies remained intact.

sentences.zh: 及光弼鎮河陽，制以思禮為太原尹、北京留守、河東節度使、兼御史大夫，貯軍糧百萬，器械精銳。

translations.literal: When Guangbi garrisoned Heyang, an order made Sili Mayor of Taiyuan, defender of the Northern Capital, military commissioner of Hedong, and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief; he stored a million units of army grain and had sharp weapons and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi garrisoned Heyang, an order made Sili Mayor of Taiyuan, defender of the Northern Capital, military commissioner of Hedong, and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief; he stored a million units of army grain and had sharp weapons and equipment.

sentences.zh: 尋加守司空。

translations.literal: Shortly he was given the additional post Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was given the additional post Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 自武德已來，三公不居宰輔，唯思禮而已。

translations.literal: Since Wude, the Three Dukes had not held chief-ministerial posts—only Sili did.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wude, the Three Dukes had not held chief-ministerial posts—only Sili did.

sentences.zh: 鄧景山，曹州人也。

translations.literal: Deng Jingshan was a native of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jingshan was a native of Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 文吏見稱。

translations.literal: He was acclaimed as a civil official.
translations.idiomatic: He was acclaimed as a civil official.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，自大理評事至監察御史。

translations.literal: During Tianbao he rose from reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he rose from reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 至德初，擢拜青齊節度使，遷揚州長史、淮南節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide he was promoted and appointed military commissioner of Qing and Qi, then transferred to chief administrator of Yangzhou and military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhide he was promoted and appointed military commissioner of Qing and Qi, then transferred to chief administrator of Yangzhou and military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 為政簡肅，聞於朝廷。

translations.literal: His governance was simple and stern and was known at court.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was simple and stern and was known at court.

sentences.zh: 居職四年，會劉展作亂，引平盧副大使田神功兵馬討賊。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of his tenure Liu Zhan rebelled; he summoned the deputy ambassador of Pinglu Tian Shenggong's troops to suppress the rebels.
