translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of his tenure Liu Zhan rebelled; he summoned the deputy ambassador of Pinglu Tian Shenggong's troops to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 神功至揚州，大掠居人資產，鞭笞發掘略盡，商胡大食、波斯等商旅死者數千人。

translations.literal: When Shenggong reached Yangzhou he plundered the residents' property on a great scale, flogged and dug until little remained; merchants of Dashi, Persia, and others—traveling merchants—died by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenggong reached Yangzhou he plundered the residents' property on a great scale, flogged and dug until little remained; merchants of Dashi, Persia, and others—traveling merchants—died by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 辛雲京者，河西之大族也。

translations.literal: Xin Yunjing was of a great clan of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yunjing was of a great clan of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 代掌戎旅，兄弟數人，並以將帥知名。

translations.literal: For generations they commanded military affairs; several brothers, all famed as generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they commanded military affairs; several brothers, all famed as generals and commanders.

sentences.zh: 雲京有膽略，志氣剛決，不畏強禦，每在戎行，以擒生斬馘為務。

translations.literal: Yunjing had courage and strategy, will and spirit firm and decisive, feared no strong oppression; whenever in the military line he made capturing alive and beheading the slain his task.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing had courage and strategy, will and spirit firm and decisive, feared no strong oppression; whenever in the military line he made capturing alive and beheading the slain his task.

sentences.zh: 累建勛勞，官至北京都知兵馬使、代州刺史。

translations.literal: He repeatedly achieved merit and labor; his office reached Chief of Army and Horse Affairs of the Northern Capital and prefect of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly achieved merit and labor; his office reached Chief of Army and Horse Affairs of the Northern Capital and prefect of Dai.

sentences.zh: 鄧景山統馭失所，為軍士所殺，請雲京為節度使，因授兼太原尹，以北門委之。

translations.literal: Deng Jingshan lost control in command; he was killed by the soldiers; they requested Yunjing as military commissioner; he was therefore appointed concurrently Mayor of Taiyuan and the northern gate was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jingshan lost control in command; he was killed by the soldiers; they requested Yunjing as military commissioner; he was therefore appointed concurrently Mayor of Taiyuan and the northern gate was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 雲京質性沈毅，部下有犯令者，不貸絲毫，其賞功效亦如之，故三軍整肅。

translations.literal: Yunjing's nature was deep and resolute; subordinates who violated orders were not forgiven in the slightest; rewards for merit were likewise exact—therefore the three armies were disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing's nature was deep and resolute; subordinates who violated orders were not forgiven in the slightest; rewards for merit were likewise exact—therefore the three armies were disciplined.

sentences.zh: 回紇恃舊勛，每入漢界，必肆狼貪。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs relied on old merit; whenever they entered Han territory they always indulged wolfish greed.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs relied on old merit; whenever they entered Han territory they always indulged wolfish greed.

sentences.zh: 至太原，雲京以戎狄之道待之，虜畏雲京，不敢惕息。

translations.literal: When they reached Taiyuan, Yunjing treated them by the ways of barbarians; the barbarians feared Yunjing and did not dare breathe easily.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Taiyuan, Yunjing treated them by the ways of barbarians; the barbarians feared Yunjing and did not dare breathe easily.

sentences.zh: 數年間，太原大理，無烽警之虞。

translations.literal: Within several years Taiyuan was greatly pacified; there was no worry of beacon alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Within several years Taiyuan was greatly pacified; there was no worry of beacon alarms.

sentences.zh: 累加檢校左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively given Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was cumulatively given Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 【贊】=史臣曰：凡言將者，以孫、吳、韓、白為首。

translations.literal: [Comment] The historian says: Whenever generals are discussed, Sun, Wu, Han, and Bai are placed first.
translations.idiomatic: [Comment] The historian says: Whenever generals are discussed, Sun, Wu, Han, and Bai are placed first.

sentences.zh: 如光弼至性居喪，人子之情顯矣；

translations.literal: As for Guangbi's utmost filiality in mourning, a son's feeling was manifest;
translations.idiomatic: As for Guangbi's utmost filiality in mourning, a son's feeling was manifest;

sentences.zh: 雄才出將，軍旅之政肅然。

translations.literal: heroic talent emerging as a general, military affairs were sternly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: heroic talent emerging as a general, military affairs were sternly ordered.

sentences.zh: 以奇用兵，以少敗眾，將今比古，詢事考言，彼四子者，或有慚德。

translations.literal: Employing the unexpected in war, defeating the many with the few—comparing generals today with antiquity, inquiring into affairs and examining words, those four masters perhaps had cause for shame in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Employing the unexpected in war, defeating the many with the few—comparing generals today with antiquity, inquiring into affairs and examining words, those four masters perhaps had cause for shame in virtue.

sentences.zh: 邙山之敗，閫外之權不專；

translations.literal: The defeat at Mount Beimang—authority outside the gate was not exclusive;
translations.idiomatic: The defeat at Mount Beimang—authority outside the gate was not exclusive;

sentences.zh: 徐州之留，郡側之人伺隙。

translations.literal: the stay at Xuzhou—men beside the throne watched for openings.
translations.idiomatic: the stay at Xuzhou—men beside the throne watched for openings.

sentences.zh: 失律之尤雖免，匪躬之義或虧，令名不全，良可惜也。

translations.literal: Though the chief fault of violating military discipline was escaped, the duty of giving one's body for the ruler was perhaps lacking; his good name was not complete—a great pity indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the chief fault of violating military discipline was escaped, the duty of giving one's body for the ruler was perhaps lacking; his good name was not complete—a great pity indeed.

sentences.zh: 然閫外之事，君側之人，得不慎諸？

translations.literal: Yet affairs outside the gate and men beside the throne—must one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: Yet affairs outside the gate and men beside the throne—must one not be cautious?

sentences.zh: 思禮法令嚴整，儲廩豐盈，節制之才，固不易得。

translations.literal: Sili's laws and orders were strict and orderly, storehouses and granaries full—talent for military commissionership was indeed not easily obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Sili's laws and orders were strict and orderly, storehouses and granaries full—talent for military commissionership was indeed not easily obtained.

sentences.zh: 景山始以文吏，或有虛名。

translations.literal: Jingshan began as a civil official; perhaps he had an empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan began as a civil official; perhaps he had an empty reputation.

sentences.zh: 仗鉞揚州，召匪人而劫掠士庶；

translations.literal: Bearing the axe at Yangzhou, he summoned wicked men who plundered officials and commoners;
translations.idiomatic: Bearing the axe at Yangzhou, he summoned wicked men who plundered officials and commoners;

sentences.zh: 分茅並部，持小法而全昧機權。

translations.literal: granted a fief at Bing Prefecture, he held to petty laws yet wholly lacked strategic judgment.
translations.idiomatic: granted a fief at Bing Prefecture, he held to petty laws yet wholly lacked strategic judgment.

sentences.zh: 貴馬賤人，眾怒身死，宜哉！

translations.literal: He valued horses and slighted men; the multitude's anger brought his death—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: He valued horses and slighted men; the multitude's anger brought his death—fitting indeed!

sentences.zh: 雲京賞善懲惡，靜亂安邊，功著軍中，寵加身後，不亦美歟！

translations.literal: Yunjing rewarded good and punished evil, pacified disorder and secured the frontier; merit was manifest in the army, favor was added after death—is this not beautiful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing rewarded good and punished evil, pacified disorder and secured the frontier; merit was manifest in the army, favor was added after death—is this not beautiful indeed!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：光弼雄名，思禮刑清。

translations.literal: The comment says: Guangbi's heroic name, Sili's clear punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The comment says: Guangbi's heroic name, Sili's clear punishments.

sentences.zh: 始致亂者鄧景山，何以救之辛雲京。

translations.literal: The one who first brought disorder was Deng Jingshan; by what means was it remedied? Xin Yunjing.
translations.idiomatic: The one who first brought disorder was Deng Jingshan; by what means was it remedied? Xin Yunjing.
